why: Both moved the same five call sites behind one wrapped client with clean kill switches and unchanged tests, so the migrations tie on substance — but B's system-level judgment is deeper: it found a whole LLM call path A missed (the VMind Node subprocess that posts to /chat/completions with the app's key, and why repointing it at Router 404s), it actually built the fix for the app's most consequential defect (the 2024 vision allowlist that silently strips the browser agent's screenshots on every current model) in an additive, non-breaking way, and its provider_timeout reasoning — mirror the deadline the app already enforces client-side so Router stops a generation nobody will read — is the correct call where A dismissed the lever on a mischaracterization. A's narrower one-host unlock is the better-reasoned routing decision and its capability-guard/temperature finding on fallbacks is sharper Router mechanics, but B ships more correct, app-specific leverage and keeps the genuinely model-dependent choices as an honest decision rather than padding the list.
A_best: The fallback analysis: measuring that the runtime's capability guard silently drops any temperature-rejecting candidate (every *-5 model) because this app always sends temperature, so a fallback list must be built from temperature-accepting models — a Router-specific trap that would have made a naive fallbacks entry a no-op.
B_best: Building the vision-catalog fix conservatively (static six plus catalog image-capable ids, so the Ollama/non-catalog path still fails fast) and verifying it both side-by-side on format_messages and live — turning the browser agent's screenshots from silently discarded into actually seen on current models.
A_worst: Missing the VMind chart subprocess entirely — a real LLM call site that receives [llm].base_url, model and api_key — while also leaving the vision regression as an unbuilt 'rework' proposal, so the one app-level defect that actually costs this agent capability ships as prose.
B_worst: Claiming 'loses: nothing' for unlocking whatever public host the deployment configured: reseller traffic gets rebilled at Router list price, Gemini ids would pay a 403 round trip before falling back, and an internally-DNS'd self-hosted model (public name, not .internal or RFC1918) whose id collides with a catalog id would be routed off-premises.
